acceptanceCriteria: The existing generated Collection create/update kernel gains Field provenance and a separate trusted values lane without becoming an automatic public CRUD API.
Default, immutable, server, and server-plus-immutable Fields produce the exact create caller, update caller, create values, and update values authority matrix in ADR-0030.

Provenance-derived create input requires non-nullable caller Fields without defaults, makes defaulted and nullable Fields optional, and treats absent nullable Fields without defaults as SQL NULL; every update patch member is optional.
Caller input and trusted values are closed exact objects, cannot contain the same Field, and reject unknown or unauthorized Fields before PostgreSQL.

Both modes decode, reject overlap, apply caller authority, and scalar-normalize both lanes. Create starts from caller input, fills only absent defaults and nullable SQL NULLs, then overlays values; update starts from the locked row and overlays patch then values without replaying create defaults. Validation, candidate Policy, and constraints follow.
Trusted values bypass only caller Field authority. Candidate Policy sees the complete merged candidate and rejects forged Tenant, requester, ownership, or other invariants.
A Mutation obtains current state through an explicit Policy-aware locking kernel read in the owning transaction; the contract does not misdescribe stale handler data as lock-owned evidence.
An empty caller patch with non-empty trusted values is work, while both lanes empty preserve the existing empty-update rejection and a missing required create Field fails closed.

The decision does not supersede defineCollectionOperations, ctx.operationTime, authored lifecycle, database-owned onUpdate, unique-key lookup, typed constraint outcomes, or the complete CRUD replacement.

Named Mutations retain one transaction, no raw SQL or transaction handle, exact codecs, locks and rechecks, candidate Policy, constraints, receipts, Change Ledger capture, and direct/network post-commit semantics.
